newsitem.title: CHINA: China moves to tighten auto sector controls.
newsitem.headline: China moves to tighten auto sector controls.

text.p: China said on Wednesday it would tighten control over its sprawling auto sector in a bid to ease excess capacity and increase efficiency.
Beijing would order all new projects -- whether they were purely domestic or involved foreign capital -- to be approved by the cabinet's State Planning Commission, the official Economic Daily said.
"This is aimed at controlling the size and number of projects," a commission official told Reuters.
"Currently, local authorities are approving projects and there has been a loss of control over the sector."
China has been trying to reorganise its auto sector, which now has more than 160 manufacturers, many of them small in scale and unable to compete on local or world markets.
Imports and flagging domestic demand have compounded the industry's problems, and Beijing has said it wanted to create three or four large auto groups.
"This policy is good for the industry overall," said an official of Guizhou Aerospace Group, which has a car manufacturing operation.
"But it will make it difficult for us to expand production to more efficient levels," he said, speaking by telephone from the company's headquarters in southwestern Guizhou city.
The company is one of the nation's smaller manufacturers, producing about 10,000 sedans a year.
The new regulations, which cover motorcycles and motorcycle engines, also require approval from the State Council, or cabinet, for larger projects, the Economic Daily said.

The notice also said the Ministry of Machine Building Industry and police would inspect existing auto production operations and those not up to standard or failing to meet their licensing terms would be forced to shut down.
